design.objective: Make release issues readable and maintainable through drawers with interchangeable card/list presentation.

requirements.statement: Read-only issue details are available from either view.
acceptance: Click title or detail control and read all returned issue fields without entering an editable form.
counterexample: Only maintainers can read issue descriptions through the edit form.
requirements.source: User-confirmed design and existing project contracts

requirements.statement: Create and edit issues in drawers with existing fields, validation and feedback.
acceptance: Original required fields and CLOSED timestamp rule apply; footer is reachable; failure retains input and concurrent submits are prevented.
counterexample: Create still opens the old dialog or cancellation mutates the source record.
requirements.source: User-confirmed design and existing project contracts

requirements.statement: Switch card/list presentation without losing query or pagination context.
acceptance: Current record IDs, total, page, page size and filters remain unchanged; switching alone makes no list request.
counterexample: Switching resets the page or shows a different data set.
requirements.source: User-confirmed design and existing project contracts

requirements.statement: Both views and drawers remain usable on desktop and mobile.
acceptance: Desktop defaults to list and mobile to cards on initial entry; explicit user choice survives resize; 375x812, 390x844, 430x932 and desktop have no page overflow.
counterexample: Mobile mode is forced after every resize, or drawer footer is clipped.
requirements.source: User-confirmed design and existing project contracts

requirements.statement: Preserve project isolation, service-side pagination and permission/error/cancel semantics.
acceptance: Read-only viewers can open details without write controls; project switching clears old details; cancelled deletion sends no delete request or failure message.
counterexample: A previous project's issue remains in the drawer after switching.
requirements.source: User-confirmed design and existing project contracts
